subject: ADR-204: the promise nobody checked -- a mutant runner for the autosave layer, and the sentence it exists for
body: KEEP prints the only sentence in this kit that a reader takes as a PROMISE -- 'Saved on this device' -- and it had 112 checks and NO MUTANT RUNNER, so nothing had ever shown that a single one of them can fail. That matters more here than almost anywhere, because KEEP exists to replace a try{ setItem }catch(e){} that swallowed every failure: if the checks holding it to doing better are themselves asleep, the kit has replaced a silent failure with a silent failure THAT PRINTS A REASSURING SENTENCE, which is worse, because the sentence is believed. WHAT THE MUTANTS FOUND. THE SENTENCE NOBODY CHECKED: make usable() return true without probing -- the single most plausible regression in the file -- and NO CHECK FAILED. A browser keeping nothing would have gone on saying 'Autosave is on' until the first write failed, which in a private window reads as a REFUSED WRITE rather than as 'this browser is not keeping anything'; those are different sentences calling for different actions and only one of them is true there. The suite's own comment eighty lines further down DESCRIBES that behaviour and then uses it to explain a different check -- prose about a behaviour is not a check on it. THREE PAGES THE SUITE NEVER OPENED: keep_emit.py inlines KEEP into EIGHT pages and this suite listed FIVE, so the deployment log, the survey design and the greenhouse carried the layer and nothing ever loaded them -- ADR-141's defect again, A LIST ONLY ONE READER READS. The list is the emitter's now, so a page wired tomorrow is covered tomorrow; all three were fine, which is the good outcome and not the point. The per-consumer blank-sheet check now asserts NOTHING AT ALL was written rather than nothing under one known key, because a renamed key would pass by writing somewhere the suite was not looking. TWO MORE BEHAVIOURS WITH NO TEST: a tab hidden or closed inside the half-second debounce must FLUSH rather than lose the last edit -- the exact case this component exists for, never driven -- and a restore the page REFUSES (restore() returning false, or throwing) must not be announced as one, since 'Restored your work from today 09:14' over a sheet that is still empty would be the worst sentence this component could produce. AND THREE FAULTS IN THE SUITE ITSELF, because a runner's first run is an audit of the SUITE and not of the subject: two mutants SURVIVED -- removing the try around the stored blob's parse left every check green, and a restore() that THREW was announced as a restore because the check drove one that returned false and never one that blew up halfway -- and one mutant CRASHED the suite rather than failing it, since removing the forget button made verify_keep time out reaching for it: no pass, no fail, just a fallen instrument, where a sweep should be told what it broke. All three are closed. verify_keep 112 -> 151; mutate_keep is NEW at 23 mutants all killed, including one in keep_emit.py rather than keep.py, because the defect this slice found lives in the emitter. TWO MUTANTS ARE ALSO CAUGHT BY THE SUITE'S SOURCE-SHAPE CANARIES -- ADR-063's checks holding lastErr to string literals we chose -- and that is not noise: it is evidence those canaries are load-bearing rather than decorative, which is what a runner is for. STILL FILED: only releve is driven end to end, so a page whose own restore() silently dropped half its records would still pass -- that is a per-page suite's job.
